title: Deactivate authenticator app
purpose: Remove the app-based second factor from your account.
summary: Remove the authenticator app from your account, so sign-in no longer asks for its code.

tasks.title: Remove the authenticator app
steps: Select [[Deactivate]]. You return to Two-factor authentication.

good_to_know: Your recovery codes are deleted too when no other authenticator remains.
Removing the app does not change your password or laboratory roles.
You may be asked to confirm your password or a code first.

items.label: Deactivate
items.description: POSTs removal of the signed-in account’s TOTP authenticator after recent reauthentication. If no other non-recovery authenticator remains, recovery codes are deleted as well. Returns to the MFA overview. Success closes the dialog.

sections.title: Eligibility and navigation
paragraphs: Requires an existing TOTP record, sign-in and recent reauthentication, normally within five minutes. The confirmation opens in the shared form dialog over Two-factor authentication. It has no editable fields; Cancel closes it and keeps the app active (opened by its address, Cancel goes to Two-factor authentication). Removing TOTP here does not remove laboratory roles or change the password. The normal flow performs recovery-code cleanup; direct maintenance deletion has different behavior.
